title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. Faces of real, identifiable women were placed onto sexual content without their consent, and the results were published as though they depicted those women. Nothing in the reporting suggests a model malfunctioned, because the material was the intended output of whoever produced it. What was missing is any check between generation and publication.

The point of failure sits in the platform's upload and distribution pipeline. Uploaders were advised to remain anonymous and were paid according to how many views their videos received, so the arrangement rewarded distribution and shielded the people doing it. Catching this before publication would have required the platform to detect synthetic sexual imagery of identifiable people at the point of upload, or a designated authority able to order the material taken offline. A parliamentary motion asks for a competent authority to be appointed to remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images, and whether such a route already exists is not established by the reporting.

What is not established is any finding against a named person. The complaints and the reports of further complaints are allegations by victims, not determinations of guilt, and the motion is a proposal rather than a law. The reporting also notes that members of parliament heard nothing for months after the initial attention, which is a statement about follow-up rather than about the outcome of any case.

summary:
Multiple female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces on an online platform that attracts 13 million monthly visitors. The videos include Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government ministers, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports. Several victims have already filed complaints or are considering legal options.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's face is digitally placed onto adult content, is considered revenge porn and is illegal in the Netherlands. Platform users who upload this material are advised to remain anonymous and receive payment based on video views. Legal experts recommend victims file police reports, which could lead authorities to shut down the website. Other options include filing mass lawsuits, complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued a case resulting in a 39-year-old man receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours of community service in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
